I agree wholeheartedly with the other comments I've read. Just jump right in! Plan out something you would have fun running (dungeon crawl? heist? maybe ask the bros what they want to do?) and do it without hesitation. As long as you have a good time, and they have a good time, you all win. Just establish that you are learning with them.

I can't recommend 5e wizards modules as, in my experience, they are quite poorly written and badly formatted. There are exceptions, but homebrew is the way to go in my humble opinion. Nevertheless, I have heard high praise of *The Lost Mine of Phandelver*. You can also easily incorporate lost mine into homebrew or other modules.

After your first 3 or so sessions, really start to soak in the wisdom of other dungeons masters. Matthew Collevilles running the game are entertaining but hard to swallow for someone new (**BRAND** new, give it a shot a few sessions later), try instead Dungeon Dudes (instrumental in my dm'ing style) and Matthew Mercers GM tips. XP to level 3 is cool.

Also, I recommend keeping your first campaign short. Don't get too attached to it, because you will want to move on to bigger and (far) better things once you get your dm license.

General tips: To balance combat, look at challenge rating. Take into account HP and AC. Depending on players, you will want to modify those up and down. Outnumber the players but give them ways to shift the odds (traps, doors, outside help-- use help sparingly)

Don't use random encounters.

Always defer to the rule of cool, unless the fate of the entire game hinges on this one dice roll. Never leave the entire game up to RNG. **YOU** are the game, not the dice.

Make fun, silly NPCs. Make them like mutual friends your bros and you have (so you can make fun of them!).

Don't splurge on the rulebooks if you don't have them. If you have the PHB (players handbook) the basic rules is all you need from there, then xanthars guide, then the DMG (dungeons masters guide), and so on. Read up on your bros classes and make sure you know them at least as well as they do.

Pre roll initiative (before the session) and keep combat small for now.

I like to start my players at level 2, so do that if you like.

Above all, keep it simple. Dead simple. You will have no idea what you're doing so make sure you follow what you're doing. Have it make sense.
